title: Attention Is All You Need
experiment: Raising d_k with the 1/√d_k scaling switched off makes the softmax inputs grow like √d_k, so each query's attention collapses onto one key; with scaling on, the weights stay spread out. This is the motivation the paper gives for scaling in 3.2.1.
archetype_reason: scaled dot-product attention is a fixed chain of stages on a toy input (QKᵀ, optional ÷√d_k, softmax), and the softmax inputs and weights are the quantities the claim is about

fixed.qk_init: for each draw, Q and K are seq_len × d_k matrices with entries i.i.d. N(0, 1), as in the 3.2.1 footnote (mean 0, variance 1); use a fixed seed so runs are repeatable
fixed.values: V is seq_len × 4 with entries i.i.d. N(0, 1); it is shown but does not affect the metrics
fixed.mask: none; every query attends to all keys

source.quote: We suspect that for large values of $d_{k}$ , the dot products grow large in magnitude
To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}$ .

metrics.name: max_weight
metrics.label: max weight
metrics.meaning: for each draw and each query row of softmax(logits), take the largest weight in that row; report the mean over all queries and all draws (range 1/seq_len to 1)

metrics.name: logit_std
metrics.label: softmax input std
metrics.meaning: population standard deviation of every entry of the softmax input matrix (QKᵀ, divided by √d_k when scaled is on), pooled over all seq_len × seq_len entries of all draws

reproduce.claim: With the 1/√d_k scaling on, the softmax inputs keep unit spread even at d_k = 512, and attention stays spread over several keys.

source.quote: We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by $\sqrt{d_{k}}$ , and apply a softmax function

contrast.claim: Without scaling at the same d_k, the dot products grow to a spread of about √d_k, and the softmax saturates toward one-hot.

source.quote: pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients
